tickets.body:
Execute the reviewed narrow Task2a brief copied below after metadata1a integration. Approved review is native-plan-review.md beside the original brief. This is read-only native capability work, not all Slice2. Writer/save2b and deferred1b stay in parent. Existing coordinator owns dispatch and review. --- Frozen source brief (historical root means existing two-lane coordinator; current root arbitrates all four lanes) ---
# Task 2a: native root binding, retained capture/read and helper lifecycle

Plan: `docs/implementation/filesystem-projects-plan.md`, first checkpoint of Slice2. This scratch brief supersedes task-2-brief.md for the first native dispatch. Read native-plan-review.md and its hardlink addendum, plus final Task1a contracts/metadata-path policy. Root has adjudicated the decisions below; no tracked architecture change is made by this planning agent while metadata implementation owns it.

Work only in `C:/Users/zFlei/repos/lux/.worktrees/filesystem-projects` on `codex/filesystem-projects`. Run Conductor context per AGENTS (registered=false rechecked). Use process-local exact safe.directory for Git. No main/other worktree edits, subagents, graphics/GPU, merge or push. Root coordinates implementation/review/commits and shared-file ownership.

## Scope and completion meaning

Deliver native library/helper/isolated runner under `native/project-files/`, a trusted Node/core adapter (`packages/core/src/project/filesystem.ts` and a narrow paths adapter as needed), native race/lifecycle tests and Node protocol/closure tests. Reuse final Task1a metadata paths, IDs, limits and hash domain; do not redefine metadata semantics or modify files still owned by Task1a. Root selects exact files/runner writer at dispatch.

2a is read-only: openRoot, beginCapture, addRead, sequential readChunk, bounded directory observations, seal/receipt pages, release and close. No .lux creation, writer lease, working save, private storage/head publication, recovery writes, Git metadata traversal or stage/apply service. Task2b owns separately typed creation/writer/save protocols after 2a review; task5 owns accepted storage and task6 owns Git metadata/absence guards. Passing 2a does not complete Slice2 or certify full project safety/writability/durability. No existing file contents are ever rewritten by 2a.

## Binding root rulings and rationale

1. Use documented parent-handle-relative NtCreateFile with one validated child name and fixed semantic operation, binding only trusted system ntdll. This eliminates repeated string-ancestor resolution after bootstrap. No caller-supplied access flags, NT path, disposition, root HANDLE or separators in a child name. FILE_OPEN only in2a; FILE_CREATE is reserved for2b. A final-path check after outside-root creation would be too late, so future creation will reuse this direct-child foundation.
2. Pin and validate every directory component from a verified local volume boundary to the explicitly selected root, including ancestors above the root, for RootBinding lifetime. Nested directories remain retained for Capture lifetime. This is stronger than pinning only the final root. A changed drive mapping/root identity invalidates binding and never redirects it.
3. Root conditionally accepts the review's narrower hardlink policy: reject nlink>1 at admission and observed unsafe metadata during seal/precommit validation; a retained read handle preserves the admitted object's bytes and identity, not continuous link-count1. Real minimal-access alias races must demonstrate byte stability and containment before relying on this rule. No continuous no-alias claim, no alias used as authority, no preexisting object ever rewritten. A later consumer must revalidate at its own precommit boundary; a previously sealed receipt is not a durable capability.
4. Reparse conversion in place remains a mandatory first semantic test and stop gate. Opening under a retained parent must stay on the admitted authorized objects even if another handle changes the parent to a reparse point. Reject observed reparses and stop on any outside-content-read/identity-substitution counterexample. The hardlink ruling does not establish reparse behavior.
5. Initial supported capture quota is a NEW aggregate limit: at most16384 combined retained file and directory handles, including root-prefix ancestors and deduplicated capture ancestors. It intersects all other file/byte/path counts. A deep/disjoint layout legal under individual metadata rules may fail QUOTA_EXCEEDED safely; this is an explicit narrower supported capture set, not a hidden implementation cap. No partial sealed success. Root must carry this new policy into tracked design before claiming full support.
6. Use128KiB maximum frames and64KiB data chunks; paginate both expected registration and sealed receipts. Hash completion is a complete sequential native read through true EOF. Caller hashes and arbitrary chunk history cannot substitute for this.
7. Timeout, invalid protocol, EOF/owner death, broken pipe or helper exit poisons that entire helper generation. All capabilities become invalid immediately; wait for actual process exit before claiming OS handles released. No detached timed-out Promise may leave a live lease.

## Native mechanism and exact bootstrap/lifetime

Build a C++20 helper/library independently of the graphics/native addon. The installed MSVC14.50.35717/SDK10.0.26100.0/CMake4.1.1 are available; native/vendor Node and FFGL are absent. Link kernel32/bcrypt and documented ntdll import as needed, or resolve NtCreateFile only from an already loaded/explicit System32 ntdll with trusted system-DLL flags. Never load a project-relative DLL or use project PATH. Test runner enables assertions, warnings as errors and bounded hidden subprocesses. No D3D/FFGL/Node headers required.

Bootstrap accepts an explicit absolute local drive path only, not UNC/device/NT namespace from a caller. Resolve the drive's actual local volume identity without reading project content; start at the verified volume namespace. Retain volume/root-prefix handles one component at a time. CreateFileW is allowed for this nonmutating verified-volume bootstrap. Validate each directory handle before the next child open: local NTFS/volume ID, directory type, forbidden reparse/offline/recall/cloud attributes, normalized final-name component boundary and physical file ID. Use the opened object, not a display path, for subsequent traversal. Reject unsupported/mounted-reparse roots and wrong-volume results. Drive mapping changes are detected by rechecking bootstrap mapping against recorded identity; report ROOT_CHANGED instead of retargeting. Root name/identity must never be inferred from projectId/hash.

Fixed desired-access/share/options baseline for semantic tests:

- Directories (including prefix and enumeration parents): FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY | FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | SYNCHRONIZE; FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE, excluding FILE_SHARE_DELETE; FILE_DIRECTORY_FILE | FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT | FILE_SYNCHRONOUS_IO_NONALERT. This is a real directory access handle, not an attribute-only handle assumed to prevent rename. Retaining it does not promise child noncreation or block all metadata changes.
- Content leaves: FILE_READ_DATA | FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | SYNCHRONIZE; FILE_SHARE_READ only; FILE_NON_DIRECTORY_FILE | FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT | FILE_SYNCHRONOUS_IO_NONALERT; FILE_OPEN. No write/delete/append/disposition rights. Reject unsafe attributes/nonregular/reparse or nlink>1 before first byte access and recheck observations before seal. Existing data writers/writable mapped views must make admission fail while incompatible resources live.
- All project handles noninheritable. Native RAII ownership tracks root/capture/kind and prevents reuse after release. Inspect file ID/volume/final path before content read. A wrong path/volume never triggers a fallback string reopen.

Use actual SDK definitions, not guessed numeric constants. If tested masks require adjustment, preserve fixed semantic operations and record the actual mechanism/rationale in evidence before expanding implementation. Stop and report any containment counterexample, not merely add another post-read check.

## Minimal semantic harness: first implementation gate

Before full helper/Node integration, build a small test-only native harness with deterministic barriers around parent lookup/open/check, leaf open/hash, seal and release. Use separate attacker process(es), test-owned siblings/outside-root sentinels and instrumentation of actual content reads. Unchanged sentinel bytes alone do not prove no read. Test-only hooks are absent from the production executable and protocol.

- Rename/substitute every retained ancestor, including above project root; junction/reparse leaf and parent; convert an already opened parent in place through attacker handles acquired before and after defender acquisition. Exercise an available junction tag even when privileged symlink tests are unavailable. Record whether the change is denied, detected as conflict, or traversal remains on pinned original objects. Any outside read/substitution stops2a until root reviews evidence.
- Minimal-access hardlink creation through native link information, not just CreateHardLinkW: before acquisition, after acquisition/before hashing, after seal while retained, and after release. Use same-volume sibling destination. If link creation succeeds, verify the reader stays bound to original bytes and writes through every alias are blocked while data lease remains. Seal catches an alias already observed then; a link added after seal is not claimed impossible. After release/next acquisition, persistent multiple links reject. Do not silently treat link success as continuous-policy success.
- Live writer before capture; writable mapped view after its originating file handle is closed; successful acquisition only after incompatible resources close. During a successful lease, competing write/delete/rename must fail and then succeed after release. Attribute-only operations are tested separately, never assumed covered by share flags.

Record native API/status/access masks and exact barrier outcome per case. No full native project-safety claim without these real races. Unavailable privilege/platform cases are explicit unavailable results, not passes.

## Helper/Node protocol and states

One persistent hidden core-owned helper per root, launched from a fixed trusted executable with shell:false/windowsHide:true and private pipes. No network endpoint. Startup hello before any root operation carries protocol version1, expected helper build identity, hard maxima and random process-generation nonce; mismatch fails unsupported and shuts down. No attach/reconnect to live lease from another generation.

Frame: uint32 little-endian payload length (<=131072), uint16 version, uint16 opcode, uint32 sequence, then opcode-specific length-prefixed UTF-8/fixed fields. Data chunk<=65536. Parse/check lengths before allocation and every arithmetic conversion. uint64 native token/size/offset is represented without lossy JS Number; convert only after safe bounds validation. Native token IDs monotonically increment with no reuse; exhaustion fails. Bound stderr to128KiB retained diagnostics (drain excess), one in-flight command plus one queued command; additional submissions fail busy. Bound both parser buffers to one complete frame plus header. Native dispatch checks token kind, state, parent root and generation for every command. Production opcodes cannot select raw Win32/NT flags.

Node public objects are recognized by private WeakMap/object identity tied to the exact child generation, not by trusting structurally forged `{token}` objects. Native tokens are never sent to renderer/MCP or exposed as physical-path write capabilities.

States:

- Helper: starting -> ready -> poisoned -> exited. Only ready dispatches. Unknown/duplicate/out-of-order request/response, wrong version/opcode/flags, malformed/truncated/overlong frame, invalid UTF-8, broken pipes, EOF, timeout and unexpected helper death poison all resources and reject pending/queued calls.
- Root: open -> closing -> closed; only read capability supported. Root holds its prefix handles until close/death. Capture operations do not imply writer ownership or .lux rights.
- Capture: collecting -> sealed -> released. Sealed freezes expected membership and receipt identity. Any partial acquisition/read/seal failure unwinds capture-owned handles and invalidates entries/cursors/receipt; root remains usable for ordinary explicit conflict errors. Fatal helper errors poison root too.
- ReadEntry: owned by one live capture. Sequential read state is offset/digest/actualBytes/eof. A completed digest is recorded only after exact EOF and byte-limit/expected-hash checks. All page/stream tokens bind capture generation and resource kind. No reads through released/foreign entries.

Normal release/close cleanup is idempotent. `withCapture(..., callback)` owns try/finally cleanup; callback failure releases capture. Callback can hold a sealed capture across harmless/injected core work for later storage integration but does not implement a commit. Unexpected death during callback invalidates its receipt; callers cannot continue under assumed leases.

Parent lifetime: a dedicated native owner watcher receives a verifiable inherited parent-process handle with SYNCHRONIZE only (or equivalently reviewed job lifetime mechanism), waits independently of the command/I/O thread and terminates helper on owner death. EOF is monitored independently of a blocked content read. Node timeout first poisons generation, requests bounded shutdown, then forcibly terminates and waits for exit; proposed graceful allowance250ms and forced-exit wait5s. If exit cannot be confirmed, report cleanup unconfirmed and refuse reuse/new authority rather than claim locks released. An independent watcher is needed because waiting for the next stdin read is insufficient when local I/O stalls. No duplicated project handles escape to descendants. Process death releases OS handles; it does not make partially read capture successful.

## Paginated operations and complete native hashes

The native boundary handles exact declared entries and observations; core owns manifest semantics. No oversized full inventory frame.

| Operation | Fixed meaning |
| --- | --- |
| openRoot | Explicit root path -> capability, physical identity and read-only support report; bootstrap errors before content access. |
| beginCapture | Live root -> collecting capture, explicit expected count/budgets intersected with hard maxima. No upfront allocation proportional to unchecked counts. |
| addRead | Capture + next canonical sorted path + expected SHA-256 + per-file byte bound -> retained entry/initial sequential cursor/physical identity. One entry per small request; monotonic unique path order rejects duplicate/case-colliding registration. No expected-set replacement after seal. |
| readChunk | Entry + exact current cursor + requested<=64KiB -> next bytes/cursor. Offset must equal expected next offset. Native hashes every actual byte in order. Partial OS read is continued up to chunk/EOF; never interpret a short read alone as EOF. Empty file completes via actual zero-byte EOF. Size/offset overflow, bytes beyond cap, declared size instability, premature EOF or hash mismatch rejects capture. Caller-supplied hash does not finalize native digest. |
| observeDirectory | Capture + canonical directory + continuation -> bounded paginated entries and observation status. Use retained directory HANDLE and validate variable record offsets/lengths. Cursor tied to capture and enumeration generation. This is not an absence lease or atomic snapshot. |
| sealCapture | Capture + expected entry count + expected-set digest -> sealed receipt header containing count, digest/inventoryHash, capture generation. Require every registered entry fully read to actual EOF and native hash==expected; recheck live handle identities/metadata/link observations. Core must independently parse held manifest bytes and prove declared closure==registered set before treating receipt as complete project inventory. |
| receiptPage | Sealed capture + opaque cursor -> <=128KiB page of path/hash/byteLength/physical identity; all pages bound to one seal/count/digest. Missing, duplicate, reordered or wrong-generation pages rejected. No unauthenticated cursor arithmetic. |
| replayRead | Optional explicit fresh sequential cursor on a sealed entry, if needed by caller; same retained HANDLE, hash a complete replay and require original completed digest. No random/repeated cursor chunks masquerade as completion. Receipt does not promise caller materialized bytes until the required stream completed. Omit this op if initial streamed sink is sufficient; document choice. |
| releaseCapture/closeRoot | Idempotent resource cleanup; no write/delete calls. |

Native expected-set digest must match final Task1a inventory identity `SHA256(UTF8(JSON(['lux-project-inventory',1,sorted[path,hash] entries])))` exactly, with canonical ASCII paths/lowercase hashes and deterministic ordering. Stream this bounded canonical body incrementally; do not serialize all metadata into one frame. If Task1a handoff changes the domain/algorithm, reconcile before writing native hash code. Core may stream bytes to an injected trusted sink; retain only bounded metadata needed to compute closure. Do not concatenate the entire313MiB possible category sum in Node/native RAM. Sink failure invalidates/release capture; an unverified sink artifact cannot count as accepted data.

Bounds beyond combined handles: expected entries<=16384, individual logical path<=240 ASCII characters, total registered path bytes<=16384*240, retained unique directory/file count<=16384 including prefix. Root absolute path must fit native UNICODE_STRING and Win32 long-path ceiling (32767 UTF-16 units including terminator/prefix); check before conversion, no truncation. Enumeration pages<=frame cap and each observation<=16384 returned entries; reaching that cap with more data reports observation QUOTA_EXCEEDED, never complete absence. All category byte limits inherit final metadata policy; aggregate streaming counter may safely use their sum for overflow checks but must not replace separate quotas. Deep disjoint supported-overflow fixture must demonstrate explicit QUOTA_EXCEEDED and release of all partially retained handles.

## Declared closure versus observations

Lease declaring manifests and all manifest-declared content. Parse exact streamed manifest bytes using Task1a validation and traverse full declaration closure in core; reject extra/missing expected registrations, dangling/cross-root paths and raw hash mismatch. Report unregistered source separately, never add it to compiler input. Whole validation includes unused managed metadata per spec.

Directory observation cannot guarantee that undeclared package entries or a missing Git index stay absent. Strict package checks can report observed extras/instability but must not promote list/rescan to a sealed continuous absence claim. Package service semantics remain a later reviewed consumer contract. `.git` indirection is never followed by ordinary content capability; future GitMetadataRoot is separate. Read admission/precommit observation policy for forbidden hardlinks does not grant a no-index absence lease.

## Remaining required tests and evidence

In addition to the first semantic harness gate, implement actual native library and external-process Node adapter tests:

- Canonical path boundaries, spaces/Unicode absolute roots, case collisions, reserved/ADS/traversal/device/UNC input; root/prefix reparse rejection before content reads; unsupported filesystem/cloud states explicitly failed or unavailable.
- Entire held capture across harmless callback; external writes/deletes/renames blocked while leased and allowed after release; same-size/mtime change rehashes; identical-byte replacement between captures changes physical identity. Read refresh never trusts watcher counts.
- Deep disjoint path fixture (e.g.256 separate paths with64 nonshared ancestors each, within240 chars) exceeds new16384 aggregate quota despite individually legal paths. No partial receipt or leaked handles. Test at-boundary smaller fixture too; root-prefix handles consume quota.
-4096 expected entries registered over frames; multiple receipt pages; malformed/reordered/duplicate/wrong-capture pages; seal rejects incomplete native reads and membership registration after sealing. Empty files, short reads, truncation, huge sparse files, chunk/frame limits and count/offset arithmetic boundaries.
- Snapshot bytes streamed to injected bounded sink; captured metadata validates full registered closure. Caller/sink errors invalidate capture. Optional replay matches the admitted digest and never reopens paths.
- Fabricated/stale/cross-root/cross-generation capabilities; closed/released entry; read-only protocol has no writer/create opcode; helper build/protocol mismatch fails before root access.
- Kill/EOF/owner death/timeout while idle, acquiring parents, reading, sealing and inside callback; actual helper exits, all resources invalidated, incompatible external operations succeed afterward. Exercise owner watcher while command thread deliberately blocked by test-only harness. Rejected pending work never resumes after restart.
- Protocol fuzz/boundaries: impossible lengths, integer overflow, truncation, invalid UTF-8/trailing bytes, unexpected opcode/sequence, noisy stderr, backpressure and excess queue. Fatal error poisons entire generation and waits for actual exit.

Use deterministic barriers and bounded hidden subprocesses; native tests enable assertions. Record exact Node24.12.0/compiler/SDK/native API/access masks/NTFS host and commands. Typecheck affected core/tests. No graphics build; no native code is executed by this planning revision. Preserve root baseline's environmental/native artifact failures separately from new focused tests.

Handoff includes exact diff/commit, semantic-race evidence with observed minimal-access hardlink outcomes, containment proof boundaries, protocol/lifecycle tests, handle quota evidence, unavailable cases and limitations. A containment counterexample stops dispatch expansion and returns evidence to root. Read-only2a completion leaves2b writer/save and original complete Slice2 open; full safety claims require root-reviewed actual native evidence and tracked contract reconciliation.

metadata.blocked_reason: Coordinator administrative stop after reported automated cybersecurity classification. No technical retry authorized. Initial semantic characterization subset passed but full gate/production integration incomplete; preserve uncommitted files and raw logs. See task-2a-report.md and LUX-P7.

tickets.body: Investigate a bounded remedy for the documented receiver input prerequisites. Use only read-only official release metadata, current local file signatures and the retained LUX48 inventories to determine whether existing Node24.20 headers/archive/import-library and the retained Electron44.3 distribution can be verified without reacquiring or executing them. Preserve the absence of historical acquisition receipts; a new authenticity check must not be reported as historical acquisition attribution. Draft one exact docs/implementation/receiver-input-recovery-plan.md only if evidence supports concrete next steps. Any change to b1 dependency selection needs a separate independent review of this plan and actual manifest checks. No downloads of native code/distributions, install, copy, build, package export, source changes, GPU/Studio/portal or system settings. If public verification is unavailable, retain the precise unresolved prerequisite and investigation evidence rather than weakening accepted criteria. This is root coordination/planning under the existing four-workstream grant; LUX48 source review and b1 acceptance remain separate.

tickets.title: Control Lux by continuous voice with GPT-Live Copilot V1
tickets.body:
# Lux GPT-Live Copilot V1

User result: Run `npm run copilot`, speak a creative instruction, hear a short
confirmation after the Responses backend changes the current visual through MCP,
then give a relative follow-up without restarting the conversation.

Scope: trusted local Node CLI; gpt-live-1; managed Responses delegation; existing
stdio MCP adapter; default microphone and speaker. No Electron/web UI, screenshots,
vision, MIDI, persistent memory, new Lux controls, or second control API.

Implementation and acceptance:
- [ ] Connect an MCP SDK client to scripts/studio-mcp.mjs; list tools and read real status before voice startup.
- [ ] Stream PCM16 microphone and speaker audio continuously through official LiveWS.
- [ ] Derive backend function schemas from MCP tools; serialize calls and return exact errors/results.
- [ ] Verify multiple spoken turns, a speed change, and a relative follow-up on the running visual.
- [ ] Test configuration, tool continuation/error propagation, and bounded cleanup.
- [ ] Independent review and relevant checks; document commands and evidence limitations.

Files: tools/live-copilot/{index,audio,live,mcp,prompt}.ts, focused tests, package.json,
pnpm-lock.yaml, and tools/live-copilot/README.md. Reuse MCP SDK, studio-session profile
rules, guard schemas exposed by tools, and Node's existing TypeScript execution.

Backend uses managed Responses delegation to retain conversation context. A small
function bridge maps discovered schemas and calls the existing stdio server; the
hosted Responses MCP transport cannot reach local stdio. Do not call Studio internals.
Use documented response.event/output_item.done and explicit function output/continue
messages. Keep listening during backend execution. Do not retry uncertain mutations.

Official references inspected 2026-09-15:
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-websockets?api=live
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-delegation
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-conversations
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1

Implementation starts at 30922c2c49693db15f18551444e9715e580f5e12 in
.worktrees/live-copilot-v1, branch feat/live-copilot-v1. API key absent at initial
inspection; real OpenAI and spoken acceptance cannot be inferred from local tests.
